teaser: An agent with a Gmail or Calendar connector can do things the platform cannot undo; a journal of every call, replayed, shows what it did and what can go back.
core_idea: If you cannot say what your agent did, what it saw when it did it, and which of its actions you can undo, you are not ready to give it a connector, and a twin of the connector, a journal plus a replay, answers all three.

nodes.label: A connector is a grant of action
nodes.summary: An agent with Gmail and Calendar connectors can send, archive, trash, permanently delete, move events, decline invitations and cancel meetings on somebody's behalf, at machine speed.

nodes.label: The platform keeps no way back for some actions
nodes.summary: The Gmail API documents its delete as permanent, Undo Send is a feature of the interface not the API, and a moved calendar event has no version history a user can open.

nodes.label: What the platform keeps
nodes.summary: Trash windows, an administrator's bulk restore and audit logs record that things happened, but none records what the agent saw when it decided to act, or why.

nodes.label: Connector twin
nodes.summary: A journal of every request and response the agent makes, and a replay of that journal into the views the agent saw.

nodes.label: Twin, not backup, log or replay
nodes.summary: A backup copies the mailbox, a log is too small, replay is the verb; a twin is an interface to reality, valued for its connection to the real thing.

nodes.label: Capture
nodes.summary: For every connector call, copy the tool call the agent made, the request sent to the platform and the response received, and never the Authorization header or any token.

nodes.label: Append lane
nodes.summary: A write-only channel gated by a token the writer holds, whose write response is exactly {"ok": true}, so the capture point learns nothing about what else is in the lane.

nodes.label: Chain
nodes.summary: Each entry carries the hash of the one before it, so a missing, edited or reordered entry shows to anyone holding the read key.

nodes.label: When the journal gets processed
nodes.summary: On a timer, on a threshold of pending entries, on demand or at the end of each session; the right default will come from a few real users rather than from more design.

nodes.label: Replay and revert
nodes.summary: A vault app rebuilds the inbox and the calendar as the agent saw them at any step, shows before and after for every change, and writes a revert plan a person approves.

nodes.label: The twin is not a copy of the mailbox
nodes.summary: It holds only what passed through the connector, so it scales with the agent's activity rather than with the size of the mailbox.

nodes.label: One session, replayed
nodes.summary: An invented scheduling assistant makes seventeen calls in under three minutes and writes a true summary that hides a cancellation sent to a supplier and a permanently deleted payment reminder.

nodes.label: Undo is a list, not a promise
nodes.summary: Every change gets a grade, reversible, partly reversible or not reversible, and the value of the list is that the red rows are named.

nodes.label: Broker, gateway or requirement of the agent
nodes.summary: Three places to capture and three grades of evidence; the mode does not change what is captured, it changes what the evidence is allowed to claim.

nodes.label: What it does to the agent's behaviour policy
nodes.summary: With the list of irreversible actions in hand the mandate can say what the agent may do freely, must ask before, and may never do without approval.

quotes.text: If you cannot say what your agent did, what it saw when it did it, and which of its actions you can undo, you are not ready to give it a connector.
quotes.why: The claim the whole article is built to defend, stated so it can be wrong.

quotes.text: The value of the list is not that most of it is green. It is that the red rows are named.
quotes.why: Why the twin changes governance: irreversible actions become a named list the mandate can be written against.
